title: Advancing SVD-based LLM Compression via Layer-Wise Error Model Search
claim: A method has several complementary components, each fixing a distinct weakness of prior approaches: sample scarcity, wrong importance scaling, and missing depth-dependent bias.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, each with an (a)/(b)/(c) caption; dashed divider in panel a
description: Three side-by-side panels, each captioned (a), (b) or (c). Panel (a) compares Sequence-Level and Token-Level (ours) calibration data. Two tall boxes hold stacked rows. On the left, one row is highlighted red as the atomic unit, with effective samples k = S in red. On the right, rows are split into small cells and one cell is green, with effective samples N = S×T in green. A dashed vertical line separates the two. Panel (b) is a line plot of relative sensitivity against remaining rank fraction. It shows solid and dashed orange and blue curves for MLP and attention energy, with green arrows labelled 'correct up' and 'correct down' and a red arrow marking wrong relative sensitivity. Panel (c) is a bar chart of compression error against number of compressed blocks, with orange and blue bars, a rising red line labelled 'increasing discrepancy', and green arrows labelled 'correct w. bias'. Red marks the problem and green marks the fix.
caption: Overview of KFAC-SVD and LEMS. (a) KFAC-SVD mitigates the rank bottleneck of prior Fisher-based SVD by leveraging token-wise statistics (N≫k). (b, c) LEMS enables effective allocation by (b) scaling raw spectral (spec.) energy to reflect true empirical importance and (c) adding a depth-dependent bias to model error depth-dependent propagation. See Supp. B.1 for empirical validation.
abstract: Low-rank SVD-based compression offers a powerful strategy to reduce the computational costs of LLMs. However, existing methods face two key limitations: (i) global rank allocation, where uncalibrated error proxies fail to capture complex error propagation, and (ii) decomposition quality, where Fisher-based estimators suffer from severe rank collapse. In this work, we address these limitations by introducing Layer-wise Error Modeling Search (LEMS) and KFAC-SVD. LEMS advances rank allocation by introducing a layer-wise error surrogate that integrates local and global layer importance alongside a propagation bias, enabling effective global rank allocation via an ILP formulation. KFAC-SVD improves decomposition quality by utilizing token-wise statistics, mitigating the rank deficiency observed in prior Fisher-based SVD approaches. Across Mistral, Qwen3, and Llama 3 model families, we show that LEMS consistently outperforms existing search strategies, delivering significant zero-shot accuracy gains of up to 4.7 p.p. that generalize to model sizes of 70B parameters, while KFAC-SVD achieves an average perplexity improvement of 19%. Project page and code: https://lems-svd.github.io
